::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Image files used in a document](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/737475/image-files-used-in-a-document), asked by [projetmbc](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/6880/projetmbc) on TeX Stack Exchange (2025-02-19; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> Is there a ‘turnkey’ tool that allows you to retrieve all the image files used in a document using the `\includegraphics` command, for example? I know that these files appear in the `log` file, but I don't want to reinvent the wheel.
:::

The included graphics files are all named in the `.log` file marked by angle brackets. So theoretically all one has to do is parse for strings `<file.ext>` where `.ext` is one of the graphics extensions.

This has an advantage over grepping the source files for `\includegraphics` because (a) a command could call `\includegraphics` on some variable parameter, or (b) some package or class command could include graphics too.

However, the log file has hard line wraps, so some of these will be split by newlines. So I wasn't able to come up with a one-line shell command to extract these.

Here is a python script that does the trick:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python

import re
import sys
from typing import List

def find_included_graphics(file_path:str) -> List[str]:
    """Search a file for included graphics

    Searches for patterns of the form `<file.ext>` where `ext` pdf, png, jpg,
    jpeg, mps, jb2, or jbig2. 

    Embedded newlines (caused by hard line wraps) are removed.
    
    Args:
        file_path (str): The path to the file to search
    Returns:
        List[str]: A list of the graphics included in the file
    """

    pattern = re.compile(r"<(?!use\s)([^>]+\.(pdf|png|jpg|jpeg|mps|jb2,jbig2))>", re.IGNORECASE)
    matches = []

    with open(file_path, "r") as file:
        content = file.read()
        matches = pattern.findall(content)

    return [m[0].replace("\n", "") for m in matches]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("Usage: python findimages.py <file_path>")
        sys.exit(1)

    file_path = sys.argv[1]
    matches = find_included_graphics(file_path)
    for match in matches:
        print(match)
```
